page: Amazon Web Services x8g.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit ARM architecture. The server provides 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running AWS Neoverse-V2 processors at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. Cache architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is substantial at 1024.0 GB of RAM, equating to an allocation of 16.0 GB per physical core. The instance includes a 30 Gbps baseline network throughput. Hardware accelerators are not present (0 GPUs), and no bundled local storage is included, requiring reliance on external network volumes.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate standout memory subsystem and multi-core parallel processing capabilities. Uncached 256MB memory throughput yields 456.97 GB/sec for reads and 211.97 GB/sec for writes, both falling into the top tier. Cached 16KB read bandwidth measures 7395.63 GB/sec. Parallel execution yields a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 25533.0 and strong multi-core stress-ng performance of 109163.03. In-memory data workloads show exceptional results, evidenced by 132.1 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and top-tier PassMark database operations scoring 46392.67. Static web serving throughput also reaches top-tier status at 125.01 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks register within median tiers, illustrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1888.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1706.79.

The 1:16 core-to-memory ratio delivers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive architectures. Applications that demand massive working sets without requiring GPU acceleration or dedicated local NVMe devices benefit directly from this density. Tradeoffs include the total absence of onboard storage and modest per-thread compute velocity. Workloads best aligned with the x8g.16xlarge include large-scale in-memory databases like Redis, enterprise in-memory analytics, high-concurrency static web serving, software compilation clusters, and medium-scale ARM-native LLM CPU text generation.

It is configured with 1024.0 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 16.0 GB per core, alongside a 30 Gbps baseline network speed. The server features no local storage and no GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight exceptional memory throughput, measuring 456.97 GB/sec for uncached reads and 211.97 GB/sec for writes, which drives top-tier performance in Redis SET operations (132.1 million ops/sec) and multi-core Geekbench tasks (25533.0). While single-threaded processing remains average, the vast memory pool and 64 physical cores provide strong resource density for enterprise memory-intensive applications. It is well suited for large in-memory databases, memory-resident data analytics, high-throughput static web hosting, and software build pipelines.
